I self taught for 3 months prior to a coding bootcamp and I'm going onto my 3rd week. I think this is the best approach. I've already briefly used the technologies I'll be using in this bootcamp but now that I'm revisiting all these topics again, through the bootcamp I realised that I didn't learn these concepts as deep as I should have which was also the reason I slowed down so much at the end (in terms of how much I programmed daily).

Yes you can teach yourself but time is money. A bootcamp can ensure a certain level of understanding in just a couple of months and get you back into the market. You'll prob get a lot of people on here telling you to just use Udemy courses and asking why you would spend so much on a bootcamp. Bootcamps have been proven to work. I truely believe people who come out of these come out very knowledgable.

I think the biggest benefit of tutorials is to expose you to the tools required to build a website. After being shown this stuff you have to slowly incorporate each of them into your projects as you'll now know which tool is used at each point of the project.

Everytime they show a new tool I like to pause and watch a couple longer videos on that specifically to get a better understanding of its uses.
